title: Chokwe Antar Lumumba: $50K Bribe in an FBI Sting — SENTENCED
summary:
Chokwe Antar Lumumba sentenced: on November 20, 2026, the former mayor of Jackson, Mississippi was sentenced to 37 months in federal prison by U.S. District Judge Daniel Jordan, after pleading guilty in July 2026 to one conspiracy count in a bribery scheme run through two "real estate developers" who were working for the FBI. He also agreed to forfeit $50,000. Former Hinds County District Attorney Jody Owens (41 months, $100,000 fine) and former Jackson City Council president Aaron Banks (45 months, $15,000 fine) were sentenced earlier in November.
Jackson mayor bribery, Chokwe Antar Lumumba sentenced, FBI sting, Jody Owens, Aaron Banks, yacht, five $10,000 checks, public corruption, Mississippi.
Photo: NatalieMaynor, CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons (Chokwe Antar Lumumba, 2017). Surveillance stills and the lockbox photo are images printed in the federal indictment.
Angelique Lee and Sherik Marve Smith also pleaded guilty; as of early November 2026 they had not been sentenced.
docs_note: Documents and stills shown are from the grand-jury indictment (S.D. Miss. 3:24-cr-00103-DPJ-LGI, Dkt. 3, filed Oct 23, 2024, unsealed Nov 7, 2024) and its notice of maximum penalties (Dkt. 3-1), as released by the U.S. Attorney's Office, and that office's Nov 7, 2024 press release re-typeset as text (no seals or logos). Quotes from the indictment are the government's allegations as recorded there. Quotes from hearings are as reported by WLBT and Mississippi Today.
question: Banks got 45 months, Owens 41, the mayor 37. Was the man at the top punished enough? Tell us in the comments.
first_comment: The ex-mayor got 37 months, the ex-DA 41 and the council president 45. Should the mayor have gotten the most time?
